passages.quote: The term states of matter refers to the physical forms in which matter exists: solid, liquid, and gas.
An atom is composed of a positively-charged nucleus orbited by one or more negatively-charged particles called electrons.
Together the neutrons and protons give the nucleus its mass, but the proton alone gives the nucleus its positive charge.
They are very small, with a mass only 1/1835 the mass of a proton or neutron.
An atom is classified chemically by the number of protons in its nucleus.
Atoms of the same element with different atomic mass numbers are called isotopes.
atomic weight of an element is defined as the weighted average of the masses of all of its natural occurring isotopes.
The weight of a molecule, the molecular weight, is the total mass of the individual atoms.
In other words, a mole is Avogadro's number of anything.
The mass of a mole of atoms is called the gram atomic weight (GAW).
The mass of a mole of molecules is called the molar mass or gram molecular weight(GMW).
Each horizontal row is called a period.
Elements with similar chemical properties appear in vertical columns called groups.
These are the metals, the non-metals, and the semi-metals.
Metals tend to lose electrons to form positive ions rather than to gain electrons and become negative ions.
Nonmetals tend to gain electrons to form negative ions rather than to lose electrons to form positive ions.
Their reactions with water range from violent with sodium and potassium to imperceptible with gold and platinum.
The light metals, which are soft, have a low density, are very reactive chemically, and are unsatisfactory as structural materials.
The transition metals, which are hard, have a high density, do not react readily, and are useful structural materials.
The most accurate observation is that all elements within a particular group have similar physical and chemical properties.
The most active metals are the members of the Alkali Family
The term valence (of an atom) is defined as the number of electrons an element gains or loses, or the number of pairs of electrons it shares when it interacts with other elements.
In general, the fewer electrons an element must lose, gain, or share to reach a stable shell structure, the more chemically active the element is.
An ionic bond is formed when one or more electrons is wholly transferred from one element to another, and the elements are held together by the force of attraction due to the opposing charges.

A covalent bond is formed when one or more electrons from an atom pair off with one or more electrons from another atom and form overlapping electron shells in which both atoms share the paired electrons.
When the shared pair of electrons is not shared equally, one end of the bond is positive, and the other end is negative.
Water is an example of a polar molecule.
In the metallic bond, an atom achieves a more stable configuration by sharing the electrons in its outer shell with many other atoms.
These forces are generally believed to be caused by a temporary dipole, or unequal charge distribution, as electrons constantly move about in an atom, ion, or molecule.
This law states that in a chemical reaction the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants.
it always contains the same elements in the same proportions by mass.
the masses of one of the elements combining with a fixed mass of the other are in a simple ratio to one another.
If two substances are placed together in a container, in any ratio, the result is a mixture.
A homogeneous mixture of two or more substances is called a solution.
The solvent is the material that dissolves the other substance(s).
The substances that dissolve in the solution are called solutes.
Solubility is defined as the maximum amount of a substance that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a specific temperature.
Equilibrium is the point at which the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are exactly equal for a chemical reaction if the conditions of reaction are constant.

Le Chatelier's Principle states that if a stress (for example, heat, pressure, concentration of one reactant) is applied to an equilibrium, the system will adjust, if possible, to minimize the effect of the stress.
Density is the measure of the mass per unit volume of a material
Molarity is defined as moles of solute per liter of solution.
Normality (N) is defined as the number of equivalents of solute dissolved in one liter of solution.
One ppm equals one milligram of solute per liter of solution.
a chemical equation must be balanced so that there are exactly the same number of atoms of each element on each side of the equation.
Acids are substances that dissociate in water to produce hydrogen (H+).
Bases are substances that produce hydroxide ions (OH-) in water solutions.
A salt is an ionic compound composed of positive ions and negative ions.
Certain soluble salts (principally sodium, potassium, magnesium, and calcium) that have the property of combining with acids to form neutral salts are called alkalies.
This type of acid-base reaction is called neutralization.
pH = -log [H+]
The pOH of a solution is defined as the negative logarithm of the hydroxyl concentration, represented as [OH-] in moles/liter.
It should be noted that the equation pH + pOH = 14 is true only at or near 25
pH values less than 7 indicate an acidic solution and values greater than 7 indicate a basic or alkaline solution.

summary.text: The components of an atom are protons, neutrons, and electrons.
An atom is classified chemically by the number of protons in its nucleus.
The subdivisions of the periodic table are periods, groups, and classes.
Ionic, covalent, and metallic bonds join atoms, and van der Waals forces are attractions between nonpolar covalent molecules.
Le Chatelier's principle states that if a stress is applied to an equilibrium, the system will adjust to minimize its effect.
pH is the negative logarithm of the hydrogen concentration, and pOH is the negative logarithm of the hydroxyl concentration.
